headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading error: ctx writes/reads filesystem and APIs while ai-engineering-hub is an unverified MCP/RAG source with no isolation or provenance controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx observes Claude Code events and can process filesystem-backed context, while ai-engineering-hub is tagged MCP/RAG and may emit instruction-like content. No shared channel is explicitly documented, but the pair plausibly bridges through files or MCP. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF ai-engineering-hub content is copied into a shared file or MCP channel consumed by ctx, injection becomes plausible.
IF ctx treats observed file content as instructions rather than data, prompt hijack risk increases.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of ai-engineering-hub outputs into ctx.
Require provenance labels on any file or MCP payload passed between the agents.
Use a separate workspace directory for each agent.
Add a manual review step before ctx acts on external text.
requires-engineering: enforce content-type filtering on MCP/file inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches filesystem, APIs, and runtime logs containing agent and graph data; ai-engineering-hub is an unverified open-source agent with no stated data handling limits. A shared workspace or copied artifacts could expose ctx-managed data to the other agent. The evidence is indirect, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace directory, ctx-managed logs or graph data can be exposed.
IF ai-engineering-hub ingests copied files for inference, sensitive context can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories.
Remove sensitive logs before sharing artifacts.
Restrict file permissions on the shared workspace.
Turn off any automatic file upload or sync path.
requires-engineering: add per-agent data-loss-prevention checks.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx has filesystem and API write-adjacent surfaces plus multiple-instance support; ai-engineering-hub is an agent framework with MCP/RAG tags but no explicit write scope. Overlap on shared files or Git-like artifacts is plausible, yet not directly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents modify the same filesystem tree, concurrent writes can conflict.
IF ai-engineering-hub is wired to the same MCP server or repo as ctx, state collisions become likely.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working tree.
Serialize write operations with a simple operator checklist.
Avoid concurrent runs against the same repo.
Snapshot state before each agent run.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx explicitly observes Claude Code events, so it can treat upstream outputs as operational context; ai-engineering-hub is an agent/RAG source that may generate facts or instructions. Without a verification gate, one agent's output can become the other's input, creating a realistic cascade path.
conditions: IF ctx consumes ai-engineering-hub-generated text as authoritative, downstream actions can propagate errors.
IF either agent forwards unverified facts into GitHub or other APIs, mistakes can be amplified.
mitigations: Require human verification before acting on generated facts.
Mark ai-engineering-hub outputs as untrusted by default.
Add a checksum or provenance field to shared artifacts.
Limit downstream actions to read-only mode during testing.
requires-engineering: implement verification gates before API calls.

E_compliance.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs and graph data, which can carry retention or residency obligations; ai-engineering-hub is open-source and its compliance posture is undocumented. No specific residency mismatch is evidenced, so this is a low-confidence, low-severity compliance gap rather than a breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into ctx logs, retention policy mismatch becomes relevant.
IF ai-engineering-hub is deployed in a jurisdiction with stricter residency rules, compliance review is needed.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in logs.
Review retention settings before deployment.
Keep jurisdiction-sensitive data out of shared artifacts.
Document the data flow for both agents.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
